page: Microsoft Azure D192lds_v7 is an x86_64 server instance powered by the Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 96 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs operating at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz, backed by 480 MB of shared L3 cache and per-core L2 caches of 2 MB. It includes 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions including AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8, alongside cryptographic extensions such as AES and SHA-NI.

Integrated directly into the instance is an 11,339 GB NVMe solid-state local storage volume designed for high-throughput, low-latency temporary data requirements. The server does not bundle dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. In architectural benchmarks, the massive core density translates to top-tier multi-threaded performance, with multi-core stress-ng scores reaching 202,853.75 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 1,146.71 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth tops 688.55 GB/sec, while cached read-only access exceeds 15,083 GB/sec.

The 2.0 GB per vCPU resource profile establishes a compute-leaning design, trading larger memory allocations per thread for dense processing power and rapid NVMe scratch space. Single-core performance falls into an average distribution tier, indicating that the instance prioritizes parallel throughput across its 192 vCPUs rather than isolated single-thread frequency. Qualitative cost efficiency is highest when executing dense parallel calculations or local disk-intensive tasks that exhaust compute cores before memory limits are reached.

Workload suitability centers on high-concurrency batch processing, compression pipelines, large-scale Redis in-memory caches (recording over 268 million SET operations per second in testing), static web serving at scale, and high-throughput vector mathematical computations utilizing onboard Intel AMX acceleration.
description: Microsoft Azure D192lds_v7 is a high-density compute and storage instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 96 physical cores, 192 dedicated vCPUs, 480 MB of L3 cache, and 384.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation. Storage is anchored by an integrated 11,339 GB local NVMe SSD, while no discrete GPU is included. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core throughput, top-tier memory bandwidth, and superior multi-threaded decompression, alongside robust hardware vector and matrix support via AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Single-core performance remains average, making the instance less cost-effective for single-threaded tasks but highly efficient for parallel workloads. It is best suited for compute-heavy batch processing, parallel data compression, large-scale key-value stores, static web serving, and matrix-based mathematical workloads.
